drip.author: borrowed_ladder
drip.title: Took every window screen out to clean them before winter. Now none of them fit anywhere
drip.body:
Eleven windows. Eleven screens. Pulled them all out this morning, hosed them down on the lawn, felt extremely responsible about it.

Did not label a single one. They are all almost the same size. Not the same size. Almost. I have now spent longer trying screens in windows than I spent cleaning them, and there's one screen that fits nowhere, which means either I've lost my mind or it belongs to a different house.

comments.author: ctrl_z_enjoyer
comments.body: the one that fits nowhere is from a window you haven't found yet. check the basement

replies.author: borrowed_ladder
replies.body: there is a tiny window in the basement above the laundry sink. I forgot it existed. the screen fits perfectly. I hate this house and its secrets

comments.author: parallel_parker
comments.body: hosing all eleven down at the same time is the part that gets me. you had eleven separate chances to write a number on one

comments.author: loonie_tunes
comments.body: look at it this way, it was a free chore. a free chore that eats an entire saturday is still technically free. that's how I justify most of my weekends

drip.author: loonie_tunes
drip.title: Froze my credit card in a block of ice to stop impulse buying. My browser had the number saved the whole time
drip.body:
Very proud of this one for about a week. Card in a yogurt tub full of water, tub in the freezer, big speech to my partner about removing temptation at the source.

Then I bought a sweater at 11pm on a Tuesday without once thinking about the freezer, because the checkout page filled the card in for me. The card is still in the ice. It's fine. It's doing great. It hasn't bought anything.

comments.author: ctrl_z_enjoyer
comments.body: the card was never the weak point. the card was a decoy

comments.author: parallel_parker
comments.body: "it hasn't bought anything" is the proudest anyone has ever sounded about a yogurt tub

replies.author: loonie_tunes
replies.body: it's the most financially responsible member of this household and it isn't close

comments.author: airgapped_alice
comments.body: you locked the building and left the password on a sticky note by the door. genuinely this is how a lot of real breaches happen. delete the saved card and the ice finally becomes load-bearing

comments.author: second_paycheque
comments.body: been there. cut up a card with great ceremony once and then remembered it was saved in three different shopping apps. the scissors were symbolic. the apps were not

drip.author: parallel_parker
drip.title: Wore my new fall jacket on the first cold morning and got two compliments. The size sticker was still on the sleeve
drip.body:
The long strip. The one that goes M M M M M M all the way down the arm. I wore it to get coffee, then through an entire meeting where I gestured a lot.

Two people said they liked the jacket. Neither mentioned the sticker. I'm choosing to believe they were being kind and not that they thought it was a design choice.

comments.author: left_on_red
comments.body: the gesturing is what makes it. you were pointing at slides with a label running down your arm like a walking clearance rack

comments.author: borrowed_ladder
comments.body: they saw it. the compliment was cover. I once wore a shirt inside out to the hardware store and the guy helping me said he liked the stitching

replies.author: parallel_parker
replies.body: complimenting the stitching is a warning shot. that man was trying to save you and you walked right past it

comments.author: ctrl_z_enjoyer
comments.body: on the bright side everyone at work now knows your size, which is basically networking

late_comments.author: loonie_tunes
late_comments.body: found this thread while pricing out a plumber versus doing it myself. I have booked the plumber. the line in my budget notebook is labelled "the cat saw it"
